summary: Heidi Pauwels is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at KU Leuven in 1983 and 1986 and earned her PhD from the University of Washington in 1994. She later held a post at the University of Washington around 1996.

Heinrich Blochmann (1838–1878) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He pursued his studies at Leipzig University around 1855–1857 and at the University of Calcutta.

Heinrich Ewald (1803–1875) studied under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and at the University of Göttingen. An Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar, he taught at Große Schule, Tübingen (1838–1848), and Göttingen (1824–1837 and 1848–1867).

Heinrich Hettrich (1947–2020) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Giessen (~1966–1969) and Saarland University (~1969–1974). He held posts at Saarland (~1972–1976), LMU Munich (~1976–1989), and the University of Würzburg (~1989–2012).

Heinrich Hübschmann (1848–1908) worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1868–1870) and under Martin Haug (~1871–1872), later holding a post at Leipzig University (~1875–1877).

Heinrich Kiepert (1818–1899) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and Frederick William University Berlin (1837). He worked at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir zu Weimar (1845–1852) and Frederick William University Berlin (1859).
Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (1801–1888) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University around 1819–1824. He later held a long-standing post at Leipzig University from around 1835 to 1888.

Heinrich Lüders (1869–1943), an Indologist and linguist, earned his PhD at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn (~1890–1894). He served at Oxford (~1895–1899), Göttingen (~1898–1903), Rostock (~1903–1908), Kiel (~1908–1909), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1909).

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler (1815–1894) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Bernhard Hirzel around 1836–1838. He later held a post at the University of Zurich from around 1852 to 1894.
Heinrich Uhle (1842–1925) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from around 1872 to 1877. He subsequently served as a professor at the Kreuzschule from around 1878 to 1906.

Heinrich Wenzel (1855–1893), an Indologist and Tibetologist, studied at Tübingen, Jena, and Leipzig under Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, and Georg von der Gabelentz. He completed his habilitation at Leipzig University in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer (1851–1910) studied Indology and linguistics at Strasbourg and Berlin under Roth, Goldschmidt, Scherer, Weber, and Windisch. He held positions at Greifswald, Humboldt University of Berlin, Heidelberg University, and Columbia University.

Heinz Bechert (1932–2005) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served at Saarland University (~1956–1964), directed at the University of Göttingen (~1965–2000), and worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1973–2005).

Heinz Mode (1913–1992) studied under George Peiris Malalasekera and Otto Fischer, completing his doctorate at the University of Basel (~1938–1944). He served as Professor of Oriental Archaeology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1948–1978).

Helen Hardacre is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. She held a post in the Department of Religion at Princeton University (attested 1988–1996) and a position at Harvard University around 1989.

Helen J. Baroni studied at Grinnell, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia under Paul B. Watt. A specialist in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, she took up a post at the University of Hawaii around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, both attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from around 1979 to 1984. She later held a post at Rice University around 1990.

Helga Uebach (1940–2021) was a Tibetologist who completed her Ph.D. at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1961–1967). In 1964, she held a position as a research associate at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Hellmut Wilhelm (1905–1990) was a sinologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1928 to 1932. He later served as Professor of Chinese Studies and Associate Director at the University of Washington (~1948–1973).
